questions.question: What is a gene?
choices: A DNA sequence contributing to a functional product
A cell structure that stores water
A protein that always determines one visible trait
A complete set of organs

questions.question: What is an allele?
choices: A collection of unrelated chromosomes
A type of ribosome
A version of a gene
A cell's source of light energy

questions.question: Which term describes an organism with two different alleles at a gene location?
choices: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Dominant
Recessive

questions.question: What is a genotype?
choices: The conditions surrounding an organism
An organism's visible appearance only
The number of cells in an organism
An organism's genetic makeup at one or more locations

questions.question: What is a phenotype?
choices: A chromosome copied before cell division
An observable characteristic resulting from genes and environment
A gamete's entire energy supply
A single type of nitrogen base

questions.question: In a simple complete-dominance model, when is a recessive phenotype expressed?
choices: When both copies of the gene carry the recessive allele
Whenever one dominant allele is present
Only when the organism is male
Whenever the environment changes

questions.question: Which cells carry hereditary information from parents through sexual reproduction?
choices: Muscle cells
Skin cells
Nerve cells
Gametes

questions.question: Why do offspring in sexual reproduction receive alleles from two parents?
choices: All their genes arise only after birth
Parents pass on only their acquired habits
Gametes from the parents combine at fertilization
Each parent contributes every chromosome twice

questions.question: What does a Punnett square show?
choices: The order of all bases in a chromosome
The exact traits of every future child
How quickly a population grows
Possible allele combinations and their expected probabilities

questions.question: Why does dominant not mean more common in a population?
choices: Dominant alleles cannot be inherited
Dominance describes expression in heterozygotes, not allele frequency
Dominant traits must always improve survival
Dominance measures the size of a chromosome

questions.question: What is incomplete dominance?
choices: An allele cannot pass to offspring
Only one parent contributes hereditary information
A heterozygote has an intermediate phenotype in the stated model
Two different alleles are always expressed as separate traits

questions.question: How can environment influence phenotype?
choices: Conditions such as nutrition can affect how a trait develops
Genes stop affecting traits whenever conditions change
Environment necessarily changes every gene's DNA sequence
All individuals in one environment have identical traits

questions.question: Why are many traits not predicted well by a one-gene Punnett square?
choices: Punnett squares cannot describe gamete combinations
They are never inherited in any way
They involve multiple genes, environmental effects, or both
Every trait follows complete dominance

questions.question: What does segregation mean in basic Mendelian inheritance?
choices: All alleles stay together in every gamete
The dominant allele prevents recessive gametes from forming
Alleles disappear whenever cells divide
The two alleles at a locus separate during gamete formation

questions.question: Why can siblings from the same parents have different inherited traits?
choices: Different combinations of parental alleles can be inherited
Parents' alleles are replaced after each birth
Each sibling belongs to a different biological species
Only the oldest child inherits chromosomes

questions.question: Assume complete dominance: T is dominant to t. What phenotype is expected for Tt?
choices: The recessive phenotype
The dominant phenotype
A phenotype determined only by age
No trait expression

questions.question: In a cross Aa × Aa with complete dominance, what fraction of offspring is expected to be aa?
choices: One-fourth
One-half
Three-fourths
All

questions.question: In a cross Aa × aa, what fraction of offspring is expected to be heterozygous?
choices: One-fourth
Three-fourths
One-half
None

questions.question: Two heterozygous parents have three children with a dominant phenotype. What is the correct conclusion about a fourth child in a simple Mendelian model?
choices: The fourth must have the recessive phenotype
Each fertilization still has its own inheritance probabilities
The fourth cannot inherit a recessive allele
The parents' genotypes have changed to homozygous dominant

questions.question: A trait changes with diet even among organisms sharing the same relevant genotype. What does this support?
choices: The trait cannot have any genetic component
The diet has necessarily changed every DNA sequence
The organisms must have different parents
Environmental conditions can affect phenotype
